candidates.classification: ReportDescription’s handwritten serialization mechanically forwards its only inner ThreatId string serializer and can be considered for an existing transparent Serialize derive.
candidates.trace: ReportDescription is a one-field tuple wrapper. Its manual Serialize calls serializer.serialize_str(self.as_str()), and as_str delegates to its inner ThreatId. ThreatId’s own Serialize calls serializer.serialize_str(self.as_str()). The pinned serde_derive source for a transparent struct delegates Serialize to the transparent field using the same serializer. Workspace serde enables derive. Therefore a derive of Serialize with serde(transparent), while retaining the current custom Deserialize, is source-reasoned to preserve this serialization operation; generic bounds do not change because this wrapper has no generic parameters.
candidates.deserialization_constraint: Do not derive Deserialize through the inner ThreatId: ReportDescription::try_new calls ThreatId::try_new and validates syntax only, while ThreatId::deserialize parses via FromStr and requires a catalog monster. Static inspection of the three pinned tracked quest JSON-subset files finds small_upright_figures in authored report descriptions and absent from monster IDs; subject to the shown build/catalog source loading successfully, blindly deriving inner Deserialize would reject that report value. The source inventory is not a catalog build or deserialization run.
candidates.negative_dispositions: Retain CatalogItem and CatalogPlacement manual equality and hashing: they explicitly use pointer identity, so ordinary field derives do not establish the same identity contract. Retain HousingMarketReserve’s nonempty all-tier default, CombatTrainingProfile’s nonzero defaults, and ExposureShelter’s Field(default) tuple-variant default; mechanical defaults would change or fail to express these choices. These bounded examples do not close the derivability lens.
